title: fix(cli): track live major in console-resolve test fixtures (10.0.0 fallout)
body:
## Problem

`Test Core` is red on `main`. The only failing test:

```
FAIL packages/cli/test/console-resolve.test.ts > resolveConsolePath version guard
     > accepts a same-major install climbed to from the project cwd
AssertionError: expected [ Array(1) ] to deeply equal []
+   "  ⚠ Ignoring @objectstack/console@10.0.0 at .../packages/console — major version
       does not match this CLI (9.2.0). ..."
```

**Root cause:** the test hardcoded `CLI_VERSION = '9.2.0'`. `resolveConsolePath()` intentionally also discovers the real, version-locked workspace `@objectstack/console` via the CLI's own module location (`createRequire(import.meta.url)`). The `10.0.0` release (ADR-0057, `sys_department → sys_business_unit`) bumped that package from `9.x` to `10.0.0`, so the live console now mismatches the test's stale `9.x` reference → the guard emits a real warning → the "no warnings" assertion fails.

It surfaced only now because the version-bump commits touched just `package.json`/`CHANGELOG`, which the CI path filter excludes — so `Test Core` never ran post-bump. It blocks **every** PR that runs Test Core.

## Fix

Derive the reference major from the CLI's own `package.json` and express the "matching" / "stale" fixtures relative to it, so the suite tracks the live major and won't go stale on the next major bump:

```ts
const CLI_MAJOR = Number.parseInt(createRequire(import.meta.url)('../package.json').version, 10);
const CLI_VERSION = `${CLI_MAJOR}.2.0`;
const MATCHING_VERSION = `${CLI_MAJOR}.0.0`;   // healthy, version-locked install
const STALE_VERSION = `${CLI_MAJOR - 1}.8.0`;  // out-of-workspace stale install
```

The `isConsoleVersionCompatible` unit tests keep their explicit literals — they test the function directly and are version-independent.

**Verified locally:** `console-resolve.test.ts` → 7/7 pass.
